questions.q: A sycotic remedy with fixed ideas, warts, and the sensation of something alive moving in the abdomen is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Thuja's fixed ideas and sensation of something alive in the abdomen.

questions.q: Sudden weakness of one side of the body with facial deviation most likely indicates:
When splinting a suspected fracture of a long bone in first aid, the splint should immobilise:
opts: only the joint below the fracture
the whole body on a stretcher in every case
the joint above and the joint below the fracture
questions.why: Immobilising the joints on both sides prevents movement of the fragments.

questions.q: The most dangerous species of malarial parasite, causing cerebral malaria, is:
questions.why: It causes cerebral malaria and severe anaemia.

questions.q: In selecting the homoeopathic remedy, which symptoms are of the least value?
opts: Common pathognomonic symptoms of the disease
Physical generals such as thermal reaction
questions.why: Pathognomonic symptoms belong to the disease, not the individual, so they rank lowest for remedy selection (§153, Kent).
Graphites is plumbago or black lead; vegetable charcoal is Carbo veg., flint is Silicea and animal charcoal is Carbo animalis.

questions.q: A mild, yielding, weepy patient who is thirstless, has changeable symptoms and is better in the open air needs:
questions.why: Pulsatilla: gentle, tearful, seeks consolation, thirstless, wandering symptoms, worse in a warm room and better in open air.

questions.q: According to §1 of the Organon, the physician's high and only mission is:
opts: to construct theories about the inner nature of disease
to explain the phenomena of life and disease
to prove medicines on healthy persons
to restore the sick to health, to cure
questions.why: §1: the physician's high and only mission is to restore the sick to health, to cure, as it is termed; not to spin speculative systems.

questions.q: Unilateral foul-smelling nasal discharge in a child should make one suspect:
opts: a foreign body in the nose
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Until proven otherwise.
